gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-gujara: Noto Sans Gujarati reads with large open counters and curved strokes that stop short before turning inward, light against the heading's closed shapes. Bushcraft feels handmade beside it.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-gunjal: Bushcraft's line looks like bent wire, thin and unchanging. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi keeps its terminals cut back with big gaps, so a long passage feels open and modern against that tight, closed heading.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-gurmuk: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads crisp, with outward-pointing terminals and low ascenders. Bushcraft's bars run at identical thickness in closed letters, and that gap between its stiff, artistic line and the open sans-serif text is the pair's best trait.

gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Wide-set, unvarying, and handmade-looking: that is Bushcraft's whole manner, a steady line with no pressure change. And Noto Sans Hebrew, with its dominant midsection and open curve ends, would carry a longer passage in a modern, businesslike voice.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-hk: Artistic and a bit unruly, Bushcraft looks drawn with one pen tip, so shrinking it would flatten its wide spacing. Noto Sans HK, a plain sans with large lowercase and lifted brush ends, holds the text part comfortably.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-imperi: Expressive Bushcraft looks traced with one marker, its closed letters spread wide and its capitals barely taller than the lowercase. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic, a plain sans with open pincer-like c shapes, reads smoothly after it.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-inscri: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian has big open eyes and a deep middle band. Beneath Bushcraft's hairline-free, uniform display letters, a longer passage in this sans-serif feels spacious and easy to move through.
